title: Choosing to Make Ten
objective: Recognize when Make 10 is the efficient choice versus when a problem is already easy enough that bridging adds unnecessary steps.
studentQuestion: Is making a ten actually the fastest way here, or is there an easier path?
newIdea: Strategy selection — the first explicit is this strategy worth using here? lesson in the curriculum.

teaching.setup: Two problems shown together: 9 + 1 (already exactly 10) and 9 + 6 (genuinely needs bridging).
teaching.see: Does the first problem need a bridge at all?
teaching.break: Notice 9 + 1 is already a complete benchmark fact — no split needed.
teaching.build: Solve 9 + 1 directly; solve 9 + 6 with the full bridge.
teaching.transform: Two different-looking problems, handled with the appropriately sized amount of strategy.

examples.transfer: A set of 4 mixed problems; sort into needs a bridge and doesn't before solving any.

mastery.evidence: Correctly sorts 4 mixed problems by whether they need a bridge, and solves each appropriately.
